A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SketchMind study, and their main text, equations, four figures, and three tables are readable. However, both reference Appendix A and supplementary materials that are absent from the supplied files, preventing comparison of those materials.

before.justification: v1 reports original sketch-assessment accuracies, single-agent versus multi-agent ablations, and expert feedback ratings in Tables 1–3.

after.justification: v2 retains the original experiments in Tables 1–3 and additionally reports inter-rater calibration agreement in Section 4.

M1.justification: The four-agent architecture, SRG scoring equations, and iterative sketch-revision procedure remain unchanged. Section 3.1 newly explains lexicon-based Bloom annotation and classifier handling of ambiguous cases, but does not establish a change to the existing annotation procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions use 3,575 student sketches across the same six science assessment items. The newly documented 890-sketch human-rating sample describes selection within this coverage, without adding a task, domain, or population.

E2.justification: Tables 1 and 3 retain GPT-4o, GPT-4.1, GPT-4.1-nano, o3, o4-mini, Llama 4 Scout, and Maverick. Table 2 retains the same GPT-4o and GPT-4.1 single-agent and multi-agent comparisons, with and without SRG.

E3.justification: Section 4 changes the reported open-source configurations from FP8 quantization for both Llama models on two H100 GPUs to INT4 Maverick and INT8 Scout on four H100s. This is a reported setting revision; the PDFs do not establish that experiments were rerun. Newly disclosed human-study settings do not establish a redesigned study.

E4.justification: The SRG and agent-modularity ablations in Table 2 and the illustrative sketch-revision example in Figures 1–4 are retained. No new sensitivity, distribution-shift, error, or method-robustness analysis is presented.

E5.justification: v2 first reports a calibration phase using ten examples and quadratic-weighted kappa for inter-rater reliability. This adds statistical reporting for the human evaluation; neither version supplies repeated-run uncertainty or confidence intervals for the main accuracy results.

E6.justification: Section 4 adds calibration agreement of κ = 0.83. All 36 numerical rows in Tables 1–3 remain identical, including GPT-4.1's reported 90.2% SRG accuracy and 4.1 human rating. No updated performance results accompany the revised Llama settings.

T1.justification: Equations 1–6, the SRG definition, and the mathematical sketch-revision steps are unchanged. The expanded Bloom discussion adds explanatory prose without new formal assumptions, derivations, or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction contributions, and conclusion retain the same claims about cognitively annotated SRGs, modular agents, improved assessment accuracy, and pedagogically useful feedback. Their headline performance claims are unchanged.

C2.justification: The added pedagogical discussion elaborates the existing interpretation of Bloom-aligned feedback as progressive scaffolding. Results interpretations and limitations concerning static coordination, absent expert SRG-level evaluation, and future behavioral signals remain unchanged.

D1.justification: v2 substantially documents the previously underspecified human evaluation: four graduate-trained educators, a stratified 890-sketch sample per rater, ten calibration examples, at least two blinded ratings per response, and explicit rating criteria. It also adds Bloom-annotation implementation details and revises hardware and quantization specifications. Code and data access statements remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 adds Reddy and Andrade (2010) alongside the rubric-mapping description and Hickling and Bowie (2013) alongside the reliability discussion. The related-work survey and positioning against earlier sketch-assessment and agentic systems otherwise remain unchanged.

P1.justification: Section 3.1 receives a localized explanatory rewrite and a Pedagogical Integration paragraph; Section 4 expands the human-evaluation description. The overall section structure remains intact, and the first-page footer changes from preprint status to NeurIPS 2025.

P2.justification: The same four figures and three tables retain their content and design. Expanded prose changes their placement and surrounding page layout, including moving Figures 3–4 and Tables 1 and 3; no new visual display is introduced.

improvement.justification: v2 makes the existing human evaluation easier to assess through concrete sampling, rater, calibration, and blinding details, while clarifying Bloom annotation. These are useful transparency gains. Their overall benefit is limited by unchanged principal evidence, unavailable referenced appendices, and revised quantization descriptions without an explanation of whether the retained results were rerun.
